newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn mulls plan to delay EMU start by a year - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn mulls plan to delay EMU start by a year - paper.

text.p: Senior officials in German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition are mulling a plan to delay the start of economic and monetary union by one year to 2000 and shorten the transition phase for the euro's introduction to two years from three, a German newspaper said on Wednesday.

The Berliner Morgenpost newspaper quoted a senior coalition source saying the one year delay for the start of EMU could help Germany and other countries qualify for the strict Maastricht Treaty fiscal requirements.
"It would be better if we could just freeze the euro clock for one year in 1999," a high-ranking coalition source was quoted as saying.
The report could not be confirmed.
The source added that the suggestion for such a delay would have to come from another European country and not from Germany.

Under the plan, the euro would be introduced as originally planned in 2002. But rather than having a three year transition period before that date, the euro candidates would shorten that to two years.
The economic data for 1998, rather than 1997, would be used to determine the nations qualifying. Germany is struggling
The paper said the idea would also appeal to the French in part because the new Socialist government would welcome the idea of more time to prepare.

The sources were quoted saying Chancellor Helmut Kohl would also not likely oppose the plan. It would also be easier for Germany if the decision on who qualifies for the euro would be made after the next general election due in September 1998.
